answer: A time-locked stake makes fakes expensive: an agent locks 100 credits in a vault run by a quartz clock, frozen twelve epochs, never spendable or double-pledged. A lantern ledger lists lock, owner key, and release epoch, so one pool lighting two identities shows. The k-th fake needs its 100-credit lock, so cost grows linearly with no bulk discount: 1,000 fakes tie up 100,000 credits, and a beacon frees only the expired lock. Lock rental fails because a lock bound to one key cannot count for another until its term expires; an honest agent locks once and redeems 100 credits.
